item.description:
Supermajority of Jewish Americans think Israel and Aipac drive antisemitism

A supermajority of Jewish Americans think Israel and the American Israel Public Affairs Committee’s (Aipac) actions are increasing antisemitism in the US, according to a new poll.

The poll commissioned by J Street, a US-based pro-Israel think tank, shows a deep gap between how Jewish American voters view organisations like Aipac and Israel’s occupation of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, compared to how the state of Israel and its allies in the US portray antisemitism.

The poll says 66 percent of Jewish voters in the US believe that Aipac’s campaign spending against candidates who criticise Israel actually increases antisemitism in the country.

In addition, 60 percent believe that Jewish organisations that label harsh criticism of Israel as antisemitic are exploiting concerns about antisemitism to defend unpopular Israeli government policies.

Read more: Supermajority of Jewish Americans think Israel and Aipac drive antisemitism

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Turkey halts Turkmenistan gas imports via Iran under US pressure
item.description:
Turkey halts Turkmenistan gas imports via Iran under US pressure

Submitted by Ragip Soylu on Fri, 11/06/2026 - 06:45
Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar says sanctions concerns prevented Ankara from resuming supplies through Iranian infrastructure
Iranians work on a section of a gas pipeline linking Iran and Pakistan after the project was launched during a ceremony in the Iranian border city of Chah Bahar on March 11, 2013. (ATTA KENARE / AFP)
Off

Turkey had to stop gas imports from Turkmenistan through Iran due to US pressure, Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar revealed on Thursday during a briefing with journalists.

Ankara began receiving gas from Turkmenistan in March 2025 under a deal to supply 1.3 billion cubic metres annually using Iranian infrastructure.

Turkish gas importer Botas had an import licence for the arrangement until 2033.

Ashgabat cut the flow of gas in October 2025, at the time saying the two countries had a short-term contract and that, without an agreement on volumes or prices, it could not sell gas to Ankara.

Earlier this year, Bayraktar said gas imports from Turkmenistan via Iran would resume, but those plans did not materialise.

He has now revealed that the real problem was the US-Iran war, which started in February.

“We stopped because of the OFAC, (US Office of Foreign Assets Control), somehow involved in this,” he said.

“Although we were not paying anything to Iran, the situation escalated between Iran and the US.”

Turkish Airlines, Pegasus and AJet cancel Iran flights as US sanctions bite
Read More »

Bayraktar said Turkey has spare capacity in the Trans-Anatolian Gas Pipeline and could easily double the volume of gas exported to Europe.

He added that Azerbaijan’s gas reserves were slowly being depleted and that Turkmenistan’s “abundant” gas could offer a viable alternative to meet the needs of both European partners and the Turkish market.

Yet infrastructure challenges, including a dispute over exclusive economic zones in the Caspian Sea, make it harder to build a gas pipeline connecting Turkmenistan to Azerbaijan.

Turkey’s own gas contracts with Iran are expiring in November, and it remains unclear whether Ankara is ready to renew them.

US sanctions targeting Iran intensified earlier this year, forcing countries in the region to take action against Iranian businesses and the financial sector.

item.description:
Turkey moves closer to Saudi troop deployment as parliament approves Mecca defence pact

Submitted by Ragip Soylu on Fri, 11/06/2026 - 09:04
Ankara must still secure a troop deployment mandate and finalise legal arrangements governing its forces in Saudi Arabia
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan (L), Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif posing after signing the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in Mecca, Saudi Arabia (Handout/Pakistan prime minister's office/AFP)
Off

The Turkish parliament passed a law approving the Mecca defence pact early on Friday, completing a crucial stage in the legal process.

The bill was endorsed by 279 MPs, with 119 voting against it. It was primarily supported by the ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP) and its coalition partner, the Nationalist Movement Party (MHP). However, the Republican People’s Party (CHP), a nominal opposition party, also backed the move.

Following the ousting of its leader through a court order, the CHP has split into two camps, and its new leadership is increasingly aligned with the Turkish government’s views.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan is expected to publish the law in the Official Gazette later this week, bringing it into force.

Under the agreement, signed by regional powers Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in August and submitted to parliament for approval last month, an attack on one party constitutes an attack on all.

The text of the agreement does not identify any specific country or region as a threat but emphasises that all participating countries will take the necessary measures to support one another in the event of an armed attack against their independence, sovereignty or territorial integrity.

The agreement, which consists of 16 articles, has no expiration date.

It allows signatories to withdraw only after 10 years have elapsed from its entry into force, provided they give the other parties written notice of their intention to withdraw at least three months in advance.

Exclusive: Full text of the Mecca defence pact signed by Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan
Read More »

Several sources familiar with the issue told Middle East Eye that all three allies had committed to formally ratifying the treaty before their trilateral consultation meetings later this month. Pakistan and Saudi Arabia announced last month that they had done so.

Turkish officials say the next order of business is to secure parliamentary authorisation to deploy Turkish forces to Saudi Arabia in solidarity with Riyadh against Houthi attacks from Yemen.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said last week that any deployment to Saudi Arabia would be defensive in nature and that Turkish forces would not operate in Yemen.

A separate source told MEE that Ankara also needs to negotiate a Status of Forces Agreement (Sofa) with the other partners and ratify it to clarify which criminal and civil jurisdictions would apply to the forces and personnel.

Known as a Sofa, such an agreement typically also governs entry and exit procedures, customs, taxation, vehicle registration and day-to-day legal protections.

It is unclear whether negotiations on this issue have been completed.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Yemen urges Arab states to deter Houthi attacks, foreign minister says
item.description:
Yemen urges Arab states to deter Houthi attacks, foreign minister says

Yemen’s foreign minister Afrah al-Zouba has urged Arab states to push for measures to deter Houthi attacks during a meeting with Arab ambassadors in Berlin.

Zouba told the envoys about the impact of the attacks on civilians, particularly in Taiz, which she said remained under siege, and raised the detention of UN staff and humanitarian workers by the Houthis, the state-run Saba news agency reported. 

She said the absence of deterrent measures had encouraged the group to continue attacks in Yemen and across its borders, the report said. 

The ambassadors condemned Houthi attacks in Yemen and on Saudi territory, and reaffirmed their support for Yemen’s internationally recognised government, Saba reported.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Low pressure in US midwest brings unseasonable heat to New York and Boston
item.description:
Further south this week, severe thunderstorms affect midterms voting in Florida, Oklahoma and Colorado

Despite the rapid descent into autumn in the northern hemisphere, parts of eastern North America have experienced an exceptionally late taste of summer in recent days. Temperatures approached 23C (73.4F) in New York and Boston, about 7-10C above what is expected in early November. The unseasonable warmth also spilled into parts of eastern Canada, with temperatures exceeding 20C, about 10-15C above normal for the time of year. The balmy conditions were the result on an area of low pressure in the US midwest, dragging up exceptionally warm air from the Gulf of Mexico along its eastern flank. This area of low pressure will gradually drift eastwards, allowing temperatures to fall closer to the average.

Further south in the US, severe thunderstorms have resulted in numerous flood warnings and evacuation warnings being issued this week across many states, with disruptive weather impacting polling stations in states such Florida, Oklahoma and Colorado. The powerful thunderstorms this week even resulted in a tornado touching down in Keyes, Oklahoma, forcing a relocation of the polling station. The tornado left extensive damage across the town, although no causalities have been reported. Officials across many states impacted by the severe weather have requested federal funding assistance after extreme weather resulted in widespread damage to homes and infrastructure.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] US midterm elections 2026 live: Democrats exceed 250 House seats as blue wave sweeping Congress grows
item.description:
Democrats widen gap in House chamber by flipping more seats, including in Ohio, Arizona and North Carolina; Ted Cruz calls election a ‘Watergate-level repudiation’

  • Live results | Q&A: Ask your questions about Democrats’ win

  • Sign up for Breaking News US email

Welcome to our live coverage of the US midterm elections – here are some of the latest key developments.

A number of closely watched contests in the midterms are still to be called, including the final two US Senate races – in Mississippi and Alaska. The Democratic candidates are hoping to oust Republican incumbents to bolster their new majority in Congress. Right now, Democrats have a 106-seat majority as we await final results.

Democrats flipped another eight House seats, strengthening their majority in the lower chamber. Democrats are now leading Republicans 253 to 157, with 25 races left to call, as a number of GOP representatives felt the weight of the blue wave that has swept their party out of power. Republicans held on to two House seats in the west as congressman Mike Kennedy won re-election in Utah and Amanda McKinney won in Washington.

Democratic socialist Nithya Raman was elected to serve as the mayor of Los Angeles, eking out a narrow win over incumbent Karen Bass, in a major shake-up in local politics that reflects the growing dissatisfaction with the direction of the city. The progressive urban planner had served on LA’s city council since 2020.

item.description:
Prime minister said his government would bring in legal requirement for companies to say what they pay when listing new jobs

Shabana Mahmood has signalled she is considering a change to knife laws, following the murder of Henry Nowak.

The Home Secretary said she had not “taken any options off the table”, after Nowak’s father, Mark Nowak, called for a clearer definition in law of what a Sikh kirpan looks like.

I haven’t taken any options off the table. I’m also not going in with a fixed mind about what the right clarifications of the law might be.

It’s important to get the right balance between religious expression in this country, which is something that many of us of a faith, including myself, hold very dearly, but do so in a way that is within what we expect of our citizens for the purposes of the criminal law.

Whether you’re a young person starting out or a parent trying to support your family, you should know what a job pays before spending your time and effort applying for it.

That’s why we will make it a legal requirement for all employers to say what you pay.
